slots.title: October wholesale inflation up 0.3%
slots.body:
October’s Producer Price Index (wholesale inflation for goods and services businesses buy) came in at +0.3% month over month.

Economists had expected +0.4%; September was +1.4%.

Year over year, producer prices are up 6.5% vs a 6.6% estimate (September: 6.3%).

Core PPI, which strips volatile food and energy, matched forecasts at +0.3% MoM and +5.0% YoY.

“PPI ex food, energy and trade” — a narrower core measure — rose +0.5% MoM vs a +0.3% estimate.

The S&P 500 finished Nov. 13 at 7,560.97 (-0.4%); the Nasdaq at 25,138.73 (-0.9%).

#economy #inflation

Which PPI line do you watch first — headline, core, or ex trade?

slots.title: 87% cite AI in Fed stability survey
slots.body:
The Fed released its financial stability report on Nov. 13.

Respondents named AI-related risks as the biggest threat to the financial system — 87% cited it in this survey, up from 50% in the spring 2026 edition.

Governor Philip Jefferson said the same day he is taking policy cues from inflation data, per Reuters.

Chicago Fed President Austan Goolsbee said in a separate interview that the Fed is missing on the inflation side of its dual mandate (price stability and jobs), and pointed to data-center construction as a large source of demand in the economy.

The CBOE Volatility Index closed at 19.30, up 3.2% on the session.

10-year Treasury yield in the latest FMP snapshot (Nov. 10): 5.0%; 2-year: 4.7%; 2s–10s spread: 0.25 percentage point.

#Fed #macro

Did the jump in AI worry in the survey surprise you?

slots.body:

slots.title: US close — Nov. 13, 2026
slots.body:
The S&P 500 closed at 7,560.97, down 31.43 points (−0.4%).
The session ranged from 7,499.40 to 7,621.78.

The Nasdaq Composite finished at 25,138.73, down 227.37 points (−0.9%), with an intraday low of 24,872.41.
The Dow Jones Industrial Average was the outlier among the large caps, up 50.46 points (+0.1%) to 52,347.55.
The Russell 2000 slipped −0.3% to 2,790.49.

At 8:30 a.m.
ET the Bureau’s October producer price data hit the wire: month-over-month change +0.3% versus a +0.4% consensus; year-over-year +6.5% versus 6.6% expected.
Core PPI was +0.3% month over month and +5.0% year over year, matching estimates on both.
A broader “ex food, energy and trade” slice rose +0.5% month over month.

Sector-wise on Nasdaq, real estate led declines at about −1.8%, followed by consumer cyclical (−1.5%), utilities (−1.3%), and technology (−1.1%).
Consumer defensive averaged about +1.1%, and energy about +0.5%.
Financial services and healthcare were roughly flat to slightly negative.

Semiconductor stress stood out among liquid large names.
$AMD closed −8.8% at $534.06 after trading as low as $520.01.
$NVDA was −2.0% at $162.85 on heavy activity lists; $TSM −1.7% at $398.73.
The 3× bull semiconductor ETF $SOXL fell −11.0% to $58.32 while the bear counterpart $SOXS rose +11.1% to $50.78.

Mega-cap tech and AI-adjacent names mostly weakened: $GOOGL −1.0% to $295.77, $ORCL −1.4% to $125.35, $TSLA −1.8% to $390.22, $AMZN −0.3% to $266.66.
$ASML was essentially flat at $1,495.16 (−0.1%).

Defensive household names moved the other way:
- $KO +1.9%
- $PEP +2.2%
- $WMT +1.5%
- $PG +1.1%
- $JNJ +0.8%

to $51.02.

Gold futures $GCUSD closed near flat at $3,886.30.

Cross-asset, bitcoin was −1.7% at $67,057.01.
The dollar-bull ETF $UUP rose +0.3% to $29.50; EUR/USD −0.3% at 1.10.
